With the New York Yankees locked into an American League Wild Card berth, anticipation is building around who will make the final postseason roster—especially after former AL Rookie of the Year Luis Gil was optioned to the Florida Complex League ahead of October.
Gil was optioned alongside fellow right-hander Bradley Hanner, leaving one final roster spot up for grabs, as the Yankees announced on Thursday. While Gil had an opportunity to pitch his way onto the October roster, a rocky, walk-heavy outing against the Tampa Bay Rays sealed his fate.
In addition to bullpen decisions, the Yankees are closely monitoring their key injured stars as October approaches. On that front, manager Aaron Boone addressed the media to clear the air regarding conflicting reports about Aaron Judge’s status.
Boone also remains hopeful that slugger Giancarlo Stanton can return in time for the postseason, as the organization continues evaluating his physical readiness through live drills and simulated games.
Luis Gil #81 of the New York Yankees throws a pitch.
Yankees’ potential postseason roster
While the front office awaits definitive health updates on Judge, Stanton, and outfielder Trent Grisham, the baseline roster is coming into focus for their Wild Card showdown against the archrival Boston Red Sox, who are facing injury concerns of their own regarding catcher Willson Contreras.
Here is how the Yankees’ postseason roster is projecting:
- Starting Rotation: Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodón, Cam Schlittler, Will Warren
- Relief Pitchers: David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Michael Fulmer, Brent Headrick, Tim Hill, John Schreiber, Ryan Yarbrough
- Catchers: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez
- Infielders: Jazz Chisholm Jr., Paul Goldschmidt, Ryan McMahon, Anthony Volpe, José Caballero, Luis García Jr., Amed Rosario, George Lombard Jr., Ben Rice (1B/DH)
- Outfielders: Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, Spencer Jones
As New York prepares for October baseball, fans are eager to watch the latest chapter in the game’s greatest rivalry unfold, with a spot in the ALDS against the division-champion Tampa Bay Rays hanging in the balance.
Key takeaways
- Luis Gil was optioned to the Florida Complex League ahead of October.
- Aaron Boone addressed conflicting media reports regarding Aaron Judge’s status.
- New York projects Gerrit Cole to lead its postseason starting rotation.

When the New York Yankees looked to shore up their bullpen last season, GM Brian Cashman knew that it wouldn’t come cheaply. The Yankees were ready to part ways with talented prospects if it meant a better chance at improving the ball club, and it has mostly paid off. After they made a deal with the Pittsburgh Pirates for pitcher David Bednar, some critics actually thought that the Yankees got away with highway robbery. But as it turns out, that trade was a win-win for both sides. And that's mainly because of Rafael Flores Jr.
Despite missing out on the playoffs in 2026, the Pittsburgh Pirates have had one of their best seasons in years. They even have an opportunity to finish over the .500 mark for the first time since the 2018 season. That success has largely been fueled by offensive breakout seasons from players like Flores Jr.
The young catcher has put the league on notice with an impressive stretch to close out the season. After hitting just four home runs in 65 games for Triple-A Indianapolis, Flores Jr. has gone on an absolute tear for the Pirates. In 43 games in the big leagues, he's launched 10 bombs and driven in 22 runs. His .910 OPS for the Buccos is also more than 200 points higher than his season mark in the minors.
For a Yankees club that has been severely lacking offensive production from the catcher position, it certainly stings to see yet another former player catch fire for another team. Similar to the season that Carlos Narváez had for the Boston Red Sox in 2024, Flores Jr. may be giving the Yankees a bit of seller's remorse. We will have to wait and see if Flores Jr. will be able to keep up his hot bat next season, but as of now, it appears that the Bednar trade has become about as even as it gets.
The Yankees needed David Bednar at any cost
Seeing Flores Jr. flourish in Pittsburgh is like seeing an ex become a millionaire overnight. You can't help but feel a little jealous at the type of season he's had while Austin Wells and Ali Sánchez struggle to supply any production at the plate. In a third of the games played, Flores Jr. has all but matched the fWAR of both Wells and Sánchez combined in 2026. The former highly-rated Yankees prospect is swiftly matching the hype.
Regardless of the price that they paid, Bednar has been an amazing pickup for the Yankees. In a season and a half, he’s collected 44 saves and his presence has really helped to stabilize the back end of the bullpen. His ability to routinely collect more than three outs in any game adds a level of versatility that eludes even some of the most elite closers.
In his 83 appearances for the Yankees over the last two seasons, Bednar boasts an ERA+ of 170 and a very respectable 1.011 WHIP. While he can sometimes flirt with danger and make ball games interesting, he has been as close to a sure thing to pick up a save as the Yankees have had in years.
Although his 1.9 fWAR doesn’t quite rank him among some of the 10 best relievers in baseball, the value he has brought to the Yankees is unmistakable. That means that he was worth the price that the Yankees paid to acquire him, even if the trade appears en route to becoming more balanced over time.
Good pitching will always be key for any team to win a championship. Preventing the other team from putting up crooked numbers is one of the most effective ways to come out on top at the end of a game. But it can be difficult to find and develop the level of pitching needed to achieve that. This can be especially true when it comes to late-inning relievers. That means a premium is usually paid.
We’ve seen the Yankees win and lose trades over the years. It's all part of the risk you take when you build a win-now team. Some of those trades hit, some don't. The Yankees needed a pitcher like Bednar to help them in the postseason so they pulled the trigger. And while trading Flores Jr. for that reason could benefit the Pirates more in the long run, a World Series title in 2026 would erase any feeling of regret for the Yankees.

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees were officially eliminated from the AL East title race by the Rays’ win in the second game of the doubleheader on Tuesday. They managed to temporarily stave off elimination thanks to a dominant performance by Carlos Rodón in the first game of the day’s twin billing. With eight scoreless innings, he equalled his longest outing in a Yankees uniform to lower his season ERA to a sterling 2.67. Given the gravity of the performance and the game, it was a no-brainer to select Rodón for our Sequence of the Week.
We join Rodón facing Liam Hicks to lead off the top of the second. With one of MLB’s best run suppressors in Nick Martinez on the mound for the Rays, the task ahead of Rodón is a tough one. Hicks has proven an inspired pickup from the Marlins by the Rays at the deadline, batting .305 with a 143 wRC+ in 123 plate appearances since making the switch from the Atlantic Coast to the Gulf Coast, which explains why the catcher is batting cleanup for Tampa Bay.
Rodón starts Hicks with a first pitch four-seamer at 93 mph, Ali Sánchez setting a target low and away.
Rodón nails his spot with this fastball, painting the corner for called strike one. Hicks must be looking for something on the inner half, because he watches it go by without a thought of offering.
It appears Rodón is satisfied with the way that pitch felt coming out of the hand, because he goes right back to that pitch-location combo.
Same pitch, even better execution. Rodón paints the bottom edge of the zone with this 93 mph four-seamer for strike two called. It’s obvious at this point that Hicks is hunting something he can pull given the bat has not left his shoulder, and this is the last pitch you want to be trying to get out in front of.
At this point, Hicks has to defend that corner of the strike zone. Establishing the four-seamer for called strikes there has Hicks perfectly set up for the wipeout slider down and away out of the zone as he’s now forced to look away.
It’s the right idea but just without the execution to match. Rodón pulls this slider a hair, bouncing it beyond home plate for ball one. It looks like a ball low out of the hand, making for a pretty easy take from Hicks.
Rodón is still in the driver’s seat with the count 1-2. He’d be well within his rights to try another slider low and away, this time trying to execute it closer to the zone. However, he elects to go back to the four-seamer, if not for the strikeout then to set up a future slider.
Even though Rodón fails to elevate this four-seamer where he wants it and ends up leaving it in a pretty dangerous place, the 19 inches of induced vertical break keep the pitch above Hicks’ barrel, leading to a foul ball rather than a ball in play. What’s more, as we are about to see, this fastball is the perfect setup pitch for a chase slider.
By continuing to prove that he can land his four-seamer on the outer edge of the zone, Rodón keeps the door open for Hicks to chase a slider.
Rodón unleashes a dandy, this slider looking like a strike out of the hand before falling off the table for the swinging strikeout. This kind of slider is so tough to lay off because it remains over the plate for the entire journey toward home, the sharp downward movement carrying it into an unhittable location. Rodón can thank the prior four-seamer for the outcome of this slider.
Look at the way the slider and the four-seamer that immediately preceded it look exactly the same coming out of Rodón’s hand. Rodón landing that four-seamer where he did set a perfect target for him to tunnel the subsequent slider. Hicks really never had a chance at distinguishing the two pitches from each other and goes down with a weak hack.
Here’s the full sequence:
Rodón is hitting his stride just in time for the playoffs. Over his last eight starts he has a 1.67 ERA with less than one home run allowed per nine, allowing two or fewer runs in all eight of those appearances. He really can’t do much more when it comes to making a case for the postseason rotation. The competition is fierce, with Cy Young frontunner Cam Schlittler starting early on and Aaron Boone looking likely to pick 2024 ace Gerrit Cole and 2025 ace Max Fried for the two other Wild Card Series starts. Even with Rodón’s recent excellence, he could be out of luck unless they advance. Still, Rodón has certainly earned the opportunity and is someone I would absolutely feel confident handing the ball.
We’ve written a lot about Rodón’s evolution as a starting pitcher to being a more well-rounded complete package thanks to the mastery of changeup and sinker. I certainly do not want to downplay this transformation and how key it is for his longevity. However, this outing was something of a throwback start for Rodón — a glimpse of the peak version from his days in Chicago and San Francisco. He whiffed over 30-percent of batters on his four-seamer and over 40-percent on his slider, that deadly pitch pairing the hallmark of his earlier years. This AB in particular was vintage Rodón, with each four-seamer exhibiting at least 19 inches of induced vertical break — well above the threshold that is considered elite — and his slider dropping two inches more than its season average. If he can hold onto the feel of this start, the Yankees will have a real weapon in the playoffs, be that out of the rotation or the bullpen.

Cody Bellinger is out of the New York Yankees lineup for Wednesday night's game against the Tampa Bay Rays, but no injury has been reported.
With the top American League wild-card spot secured and Aaron Judge sidelined, the open question is how many at-bats Bellinger takes into a best-of-three series that starts in six days, most likely against the Boston Red Sox.
José Caballero moves into left field against Rays right-hander Mason Englert, according to CBS Sports. The site found nothing pointing to a physical problem and characterized the absence as a pre-playoff day off.
The timing follows a cold stretch. Bellinger opened September by hitting .373 through his first 14 games of the month, then managed just three hits in his next 20 at-bats.
He managed to come through on Tuesday. His fourth-inning, two-run homer off Nick Martinez, his 17th of the season, was the only scoring in a 2-0 Game 1 win before Tampa Bay took the nightcap of a doubleheader 6-1 and clinched the American League East.

Yankees Rest Plan Includes Cody Bellinger
After the doubleheader, manager Aaron Boone singled out Bellinger, catcher Austin Wells and outfielder Spencer Jones as regulars due for rest over the final week, according to Yankees beat writer Gary Phillips.
"As best we can, we'll get ourselves sharp. They're real games, so we're playing, but I definitely will pick some spots to get some guys down. Some of our leverage guys in the 'pen, we want them pitching, but we'll be very selective in how we do it," Boone said as quoted by MLB.com's Bryan Hoch.
Gerrit Cole starts Wednesday, and Cam Schlittler follows Thursday before a three-game series against the Baltimore Orioles closes the schedule, according to Hoch.
At 90-67, New York holds the No. 4 seed and will host the No. 5 seed in the Wild Card Series opening Sept. 29, according to MLB.com. The Boston Red Sox, at 84-73, are the likeliest opponent.
Judge will not be part of it. Boone said the captain has a "moderate" right calf strain and is not expected back for that round, according to Hoch.
"Missing Judge, it hurts. We all know he's the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is, we're going to have to find a way," Bellinger said, as quoted by Hoch.
Bellinger Career Resume
Bellinger's September line sits at .338/.351/.581 with five homers and 14 RBI, according to Yardbarker. He has appeared in 76 playoff games, hitting 10 homers and driving in 37 runs.
Bellinger was born July 13, 1995, in Scottsdale, Arizona. The Los Angeles Dodgers drafted him in the fourth round in 2013, straight out of Chandler's Hamilton High School. He won National League Rookie of the Year in 2017 and NL MVP in 2019, when he hit .305 with 47 homers.
His path also runs through a 2020 World Series title with the Dodgers and two seasons with the Chicago Cubs. New York acquired him in a December 2024 trade and, after a 2025 season of 29 homers and 98 RBI, re-signed him in January to a five-year, $162.5 million contract that gives him two opt-out chances and full no-trade protection, according to Bronx Pinstripes.
Limited to 130 games by a 25-game injured-list stint for a left hamstring strain, Bellinger is hitting .268 this season with 17 homers, 73 RBI and 12 stolen bases. His career totals stand at 242 home runs and 768 RBI.

Updated Yankees projected Wild Card Series roster without Aaron Judge
NEW YORK - Here was the scenario these Yankees hoped to avoid, but couldn't - a triumphant Tampa Bay Rays team, celebrating their AL East title on Bronx turf.
"They've put together a fantastic regular season to earn that,'' said manager Aaron Boone, after the Rays' 6-1 victory in Tuesday's nightcap of a split doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
"Hopefully, we get another crack at them.''
That would be in a best-of-five AL Division Series, but only if the Yankees advance from a best-of-three Wild Card series, which they'll host - likely against the rival Red Sox.
With that Wild Card opponent in mind, here is our updated version of a Yankees 26-man playoff roster (12 pitchers, 14 position players), for a series that would begin on Tuesday, Sept. 29.
Rosters can be altered before each postseason round. Injured players can be replaced in-series (pitcher for pitcher, position player for position player) but the injured player is ineligible for the next playoff series.
Projected Yankees pitchers (12)
Starters (3): RHPs Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole; LHP Max Fried.
Relievers (9): RHPs David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Will Warren, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber; LHPs Ryan Weathers, Tim Hill, Brent Headrick, Carlos Rodon.
On the bubble: RHPs Clarke Schmidt.
Also available: RHPs Luis Gil, Elmer Rodriguez, Yerry de los Santos, Bradley Hanner, Carlos Lagrange; LHP Ryan Yarbrough.
Currently injured: RHPs Fernando Cruz, Angel Chivilli, Kervin Castro.
Analysis: Would the Yanks start anyone but Schlittler in Game 1?
Well, nothing's been firmly stated about the first round rotation, though Schlittler - the odds-on choice for the AL Cy Young Award - would be on normal rest for the opener.
Cole (Wednesday) and Schlittler (Thursday) will make their final regular season starts during this Rays series, though Boone mentioned limiting both starters in these tune-ups for postseason.
In the bullpen, Schmidt's recent bout of biceps cramping wasn't fully resolved as of Tuesday; he was due to be re-examined after a throwing session.
It's possible that even a slight setback takes Schmidt out of consideration for an important playoff spot, moving Michael Fulmer off the bubble and on the roster.
Rodon's eight shutout innings in Tuesday's doubleheader opener was his best effort, during an impressive stretch drive.
He'd be certain to start Game 1 or 2 of a Division Series vs. the Rays, but the Yanks might need his services - in some capacity - to advance vs. Boston, so he's now included here.
Projected Yankees infielders, utility/DH (9)
Infielders (7): Luis Garcia Jr., 1B; Paul Goldschmidt, 1B; Ben Rice, 1B-DH; Jazz Chisholm Jr., 2B; George Lombard Jr., SS; Anthony Volpe, 2B-SS; Ryan McMahon, 3B.
Utility players: (2): Jose Caballero, IF-OF; Amed Rosario, 3B-2B.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: Max Schuemann.
Analysis: Garcia and McMahon are slumping at the wrong time, while Chisholm - who just returned off the IL (right thumb sprain) on Tuesday - has this week to find his rhythm again at the plate.
But that trio of lefty hitters might all be starting on the bench against Boston, which could employ three lefty starters against the Yanks.
That puts Caballero in play as a third base option, with the veteran Goldschmidt (.997 OPS vs. lefties) at first base, the rookie Lombard at short, and Volpe recast as a second baseman.
Projected Yankees outfielders (3)
Cody Bellinger, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: Jasson Dominguez.
Currently injured: Aaron Judge, Trent Grisham.
Analysis: That's a thin outfield without Judge, whom the Yanks are not planning to have for at least the Wild Card series - per Boone - due to the captain's "moderate'' right calf strain.
It's increasingly unlikely that Grisham (strained hamstring) is available, too, by next week, and that presents a danger considering Ramos' defensive deficiencies.
For that same reason, Dominguez is on the outside. Mostly, the Yanks need the potent right-handed bats of Ramos (who has found his hitting groove) and Rosario to combat Boston's lefty pitching.
Caballero could find himself pressed into outfield duty, too.
Without Judge, "it's going to be super tough on us,'' said Ramos. "But we're going to go forward, for sure.''
Yankees' projected catchers (2)
Austin Wells, Ali Sanchez.
On the bubble: None.
Also available: J.C. Escarra.
Analysis: Wells has been a better offensive presence after a brutal first half, and Sanchez has learned the staff and he earned much praise from Rodon for his contribution to Tuesday's game one win.
Boone has kept the Cole-Wells pairing together, and you'd still anticipate Wells getting starts vs. Boston's lefty starters throughout this opening series.

Chisholm’s most memorable moment, though, was failing to cover first base on a safety squeeze in the 6-1 loss in The Bronx that helped the Rays clinch the division.
With one out and runners on the corners in the seventh inning and Taylor Walls at the plate, manager Aaron Boone said the Yankees were aware that a bunt would be coming “more often than not.”
And sure enough, Walls pushed a bunt toward first base, and Luis García Jr. charged, as he was supposed to, Boone said.
Chisholm started to run over but stopped, believing García would halt his charge and return to the base. Chisholm instead hovered by second base.
“He’s just gotta go [to first base] every time, and he knows that,” Boone said of Chisholm, who acknowledged the mistake.
“Next time, I’ll just keep going through,” said Chisholm, who was sidelined for two weeks after spraining his right thumb Sept. 8 and has returned to a team sorting out its infield with five games to go before the postseason.
Asked before the doubleheader if Volpe would continue to get time at second with Chisholm back, Boone said, “We’ll see.”
Chisholm went 1-for-3 with a single and a walk, while Volpe went 0-for-3 with three strikeouts in the 2-0 doubleheader opener. Entering play, Volpe had hit .286 with a .753 OPS in 10 games with Chisholm on the IL.
The Yankees also have to figure out third base, as Ryan McMahon is a mess on both sides of the ball.
José Caballero got the start there in the opener against Martinez and went 1-for-3 with a pair of stolen bases, with lefty-swinging McMahon in the lineup for the nightcap against Drew Rasmussen. McMahon went 0-for-2 with a strikeout and could not make a difficult play on a Nick Fortes chopper that reached McMahon on an in-between hop and went for an infield single.
Boone said he wanted to get “regular reps” for both Caballero and McMahon, who entered Tuesday just 6-for-40 with an OPS of .402 since returning from a sprained thumb Sept. 1.
Amed Rosario, signed in the offseason with the idea of playing third against lefties, has not produced in those situations this year, and the Yankees have mostly gone with Caballero and McMahon over the last three weeks.
To make room on the roster for Chisholm, Max Schuemann was optioned to the FCL Yankees.
Clarke Schmidt played catch Tuesday after experiencing cramping in his biceps while warming up during Sunday’s game against Arizona.
Boone said the team was awaiting word from doctors regarding the right-hander’s availability, but a source told The Post’s Joel Sherman that Schmidt still felt something in the area.
Another source said an IL stint isn’t out of the question as Schmidt is trying to earn a spot on the postseason roster after missing over a year following Tommy John surgery.
Ryan Weathers threw a bullpen session between games as he works to return from a left forearm strain, and Fernando Cruz (UCL) played catch.
The Yankees haven’t announced their playoff rotation, but Gerrit Cole has started the team’s first postseason game in every season in which he’s been healthy since he joined the organization in 2020.
The right-hander will start Wednesday and was asked by The Post how he would feel if Cam Schlittler got the start in the first game of a wild-card series this season.
“Fine by me,’’ said Cole, who had a similar reaction when there was discussion of having Nestor Cortes open the playoffs in 2022. “What matters is me trying to be my best. Whatever [Boone] thinks is good.”

The New York Yankees are coming off two straight losses in Arizona to the Diamondbacks, a setback that left them a full six games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East pennant race.
But the Yankees still have a chance to win the division and with it, the top seed in the AL and a bye out of the Wild card playoff round.
The Yankees and Rays open a four-game, head-to-head series with the first game of a doubleheader Tuesday at Yankee Stadium. With a four-game sweep, the Yankees would take the season tiebreaker and need to win at least two of three against the Baltimore Orioles, while the Rays lose two of three to the Philadelphia Phillies to close out the regular season.
Before Game One of the twin bill, the Yankees announced a decision on how they will utilize veteran first basinal Paul Goldschmidt.
Goldschmidt is out of the New York Yankees lineup for a third straight game, sidelined again by a stark platoon split against right-handed pitching.
The pattern has held all September, and it likely has fans wondering about how much longer the 39-year-old holds even a part-time role with October two weeks away.

Boone's Platoon Explains Goldschmidt Sit
Aaron Boone's lineup card for Tuesday's series opener against Tampa Bay leaves Goldschmidt out again, extending a run that traces back to Saturday. He started Friday against left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez in Arizona and went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs, then sat both weekend games against right-handers Brandon Pfaadt and Corbin Burnes. That's three benchings in the last three games against right-handed starters.
Why? Goldschmidt has produced an elite 1.006 OPS against lefties this season but an anemic a .572 mark versus right-handers, a gap wide enough that Boone starts Ben Rice at DH and Luis García Jr. at first whenever a right-hander pitches. An Athletic report on the lineup moves after Aaron Judge's calf strain named Goldschmidt and Heliot Ramos as the bats Boone leans on against lefties, with García handling the right-handed side.
Nick Martinez, Tuesday's Tampa Bay starter, has largely dominated Goldschmidt in his career. The former National League MVP is 2-for-10 with four walks and two strikeouts against Martinez, and he is 0-for-13 with four strikeouts in his last three meetings with the right-hander since 2024. Martinez enters at 15-4 with a 2.94 ERA this year, and beat the Yankees in the Bronx in May, giving Boone both the season splits and the head-to-head history pointing toward a Goldschmidt benching.
Tuesday's day-night doubleheader against two more right-handed Rays starters gives Boone an easy excuse to sit the 39-year-old.

Goldschmidt's Future in New York
Goldschmidt turns free agent again this winter, and the Yankees have made no public commitment either way. A cheap return as a lefty-masher and clubhouse mentor remains plausible given Rice's grip on first base, and his credentials, a 2022 NL MVP award, seven All-Star selections, four Gold Gloves and five Silver Sluggers still makes him a name teams will inquire about this winter.
First base belongs to Rice, who has grown into an everyday role with 39 home runs and 95 RBI this season, pushing Goldschmidt into a complementary, short-side platoon job. That role fits the final stretch of a one-year, $4 million contract that can grow by $500,000 at each of four plate-appearance thresholds, according to Spotrac, a modest deal compared with the $12.5 million he earned in his first Yankees season a year earlier.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Varias latas de cerveza fueron vaciadas sobre la cabeza de Aaron Judge mientras el capitán de los Yankees permanecía en el centro del clubhouse de visitantes en el Target Field la semana pasada, rodeado de compañeros eufóricos que celebraban la clasificación del club a la postemporada.
Judge entrecerró los ojos por el ardor y les advirtió a sus compañeros: “Me las van a pagar”.
Aun así, no pretenden que ésa sea su última celebración, pues tienen un firme control del primer puesto del Comodín de la Liga Americana y el título del Este de la Liga Americana todavía está en juego.
“Siempre es bueno cuando puedes celebrar esos momentos durante una temporada”, dijo el manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone. “Mucha gente dedica mucho tiempo, esfuerzo y sudor. Obviamente, éste es apenas el primer paso de lo que esperamos sean muchos”.
Ahora que aseguraron su pase a la postemporada, ¿qué más les espera a los Yankees?
¿Cómo podría quedar el roster para la postemporada?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez 
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Trent Grisham, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos
BD: Ben Rice
LA: Gerrit Cole, Cam Schlittler, Max Fried
R: David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick, Tim Hill, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber, Will Warren, Carlos Rodón
Los Yankees utilizaron a 12 lanzadores y a 14 bateadores cuando recibieron a los Medias Rojas en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, así que partiremos de esa misma premisa para el 2026.
Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles contra Tampa Bay, mientras que Schlittler lo hará el jueves. Mirando hacia adelante, eso sugiere que Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Es posible que los Yankees estén alineando a Cole para abrir el Juego 1 y a Schlittler para el Juego 2. Hasta ahora, han preferido no decir mucho al respecto, salvo por la confirmación de Boone de que Cole realizará una apertura en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Rodón podría estar en el bullpen para la serie. En nuestra proyección del roster lo tenemos activo, mientras que el dominicano Luis Gil y Ryan Yarbrough figuran entre quienes quedarían fuera. Ryan Weathers trabaja para regresar como relevista, pero el tiempo juega en su contra. Si está saludable, podría ocupar el lugar de Fulmer o Schreiber.
Chisholm espera regresar esta semana para la serie contra los Rays tras sufrir un esguince en el pulgar derecho, mientras que Grisham ha mostrado mejoría y podría quedarse con un puesto en los jardines. De no ser así, Max Schuemann está entre las alternativas. Otro aspecto para seguir: ¿Podrían los Yankees incluir a Anthony Volpe en lugar de Rosario? Es una posibilidad que vale la pena considerar.
¿Cuándo comenzará la postemporada?
Si los Yankees terminan disputando la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, ésta empezará el 29 de septiembre. La Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana arrancará el 3 de octubre.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees si la temporada terminara hoy?
En estos momentos, sería una revancha de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, con los Yankees recibiendo a los Medias Rojas en el Bronx. Los Yankees ganaron aquella serie dos victorias por una.
Este año, los Yankees tuvieron marca de 7-6 contra Boston.
¿Todavía pueden ganar el Este de la Liga Americana?
Sí, pero tienen un camino cuesta arriba. Los Yankees tienen por delante cuatro enfrentamientos directos con los Rays a partir del martes en el Yankee Stadium, incluyendo una doble-cartelera para abrir la serie. Tampa Bay domina actualmente la serie particular por 6-3, lo que significa que los Yankees necesitarían barrer para quedarse con el criterio de desempate entre ambos.
¿Quién abriría el Juego 1 por los Yankees?
Como se mencionó anteriormente, Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles frente a Tampa Bay y Schlittler lo hará al día siguiente. Por lo tanto, Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Después de permitir siete jonrones en sus dos aperturas anteriores, Cole mermó las dudas externas sobre una posible apertura en los playoffs con una sólida actuación en Arizona. Fried y Rodón han lidiado con lesiones, pero están recuperando su mejor nivel en el momento indicado.
Warren realizará una apertura más durante la serie contra los Orioles, según Boone, pero llegará a los playoffs como una interesante alternativa para el relevo.
¿Será Judge un factor en los playoffs?
Los Yankees han sido poco específicos sobre el estado de Judge. Boone ha evitado ofrecer un plazo estimado para su recuperación e incluso revelar el grado del tirón en la pantorrilla derecha. En términos generales, hasta un tirón de Grado 1, el de menor gravedad, requiere de dos a tres semanas para una recuperación completa.
Es casi seguro que Judge intentará regresar antes. La primera fecha en la que podría ser activado sería para el Juego 162, el 27 de septiembre. Tal como está el panorama ahora mismo, existe una posibilidad muy real de que los Yankees no cuenten con Judge al menos para una potencial Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Judge dijo que le “gustaría” estar activo para la postemporada y que ése es “el plan”, pero no dijo necesariamente que sería para el 29 de septiembre.
¿Cuáles son las otras preocupaciones en cuanto a lesiones?
Grisham ha avanzado en su programa progresivo de correr y debe de estar disponible para el roster de los playoffs, aunque Boone dijo que no será activado antes de que termine la temporada regular. Chisholm ha estado bateando y realizando tiros, y debe de ser activado durante la serie contra los Rays. Si sufre algún contratiempo, Volpe entraría en consideración.
Y aunque los Yankees no han descartado a Giancarlo Stanton, quien ha estado bateando, han ofrecido pocas novedades sobre su recuperación del más reciente tirón en la pantorrilla.

item.content:encoded:
Shortly after getting walked-off by the Diamondbacks on Saturday night, the Yankees acknowledged their reality.
“Mathematically, [it’s] probably pretty tough, but you never know,” Cody Bellinger said of winning the American League East.
Unable to bounce back with an 8-4 loss in Sunday’s series finale against Arizona, the second-place Yankees are now six games back of the division-leading Rays with seven games left in the regular season. The rivals will play four of those games against each other at Yankee Stadium this week, starting with a doubleheader on Tuesday.
Aaron Boone acknowledged that his team will probably have to sweep the Rays just for a crack at the division crown, as FanGraphs gave the Yankees a measly 2.7% chance of winning the AL East before Sunday’s game.
“There’s still a chance,” Cam Schlittler said, “but we gotta play our asses off a little bit.”
While the Yankees still technically have a shot to defy the odds, the far likelier scenario is that their postseason begins on Sept. 29 at home against Boston in the Wild Card round for the second straight year.
With that in mind, let’s try to predict what the club’s roster could look like for that series.
Hitters (15): Ben Rice, Heliot Ramos, Spencer Jones, Trent Grisham, Cody Bellinger, Ryan McMahon, George Lombard Jr., Paul Goldschmidt, Luis García Jr., Jazz Chisholm Jr., José Caballero, Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez, Anthony Volpe, Amed Rosario
With the Yankees providing minimal info on Aaron Judge’s calf strain, it can’t be assumed he’ll be available.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. could return from a sprained thumb as soon as Tuesday. Meanwhile, Trent Grisham is still in play as a playoff option as he recovers from a hamstring strain, but Boone said that activating him before the end of the regular season is “complicated,” partly due to roster logistics.
With Max Schuemann presumably the corresponding move for Chisholm, the Yankees would have to option someone else if they activated Grisham before the playoffs. That someone wouldn’t be able to be recalled for 10 days barring a new injury; it seems like Jasson Domínguez is being protected from that window in case he’s needed for the Wild Card roster.
Grisham has been doing baseball activities and is “pretty deep into his running progression,” Boone said. If he is on the Wild Card roster, the Yankees will have an interesting decision to make between him and Spencer Jones in center field.
Third base could also be a conundrum, as Ryan McMahon and José Caballero don’t offer much offensively, and Amed Rosario is a poor defender. He’s only on the roster as an option against lefties, even though he hasn’t been great against them.
Another idea would be to use Volpe, who has been playing second, at third against lefties since he played a few games there in the minors this season. However, he doesn’t have a strong arm, and he hasn’t been working at third base since being recalled. Volpe said that the Yankees have not talked to him about manning the hot corner before the regular season ends.
“We’ll see,” Boone said. “First things first, getting Jazz back, and then we’ll figure out as the week unfolds how I want to play it.”
Volpe can also play second over Chisholm against lefties.
Pitchers (11): Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Will Warren, David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, Clarke Schmidt, John Schreiber, Tim Hill, Ryan Weathers
As things stand, Carlos Rodón, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are scheduled to pitch against the Rays, in that order. That would give Cole, who has struggled to get swing-and-miss, an extra day of rest if he were to start Game 1 of the Wild Card round. Schlittler, the AL Cy Young frontrunner, would be on regular rest if tabbed for Game 1.
Because the Wild Card round is a best-of-three series, Rodón isn’t needed, especially with Will Warren expected to work out of the bullpen and able to provide length.
Warren, slated to make one more start this season after struggling on Sunday, is one of a few converted starters who could impact the Bombers’ bullpen this postseason. Clarke Schmidt and Ryan Weathers are the others. Schmidt, being cautious in his return from Tommy John surgery, couldn’t come into Sunday’s game due to some bicep cramping, while Weathers isn’t expected to return from a flexor strain before the regular season ends.
Still, neither Boone nor pitching coach Matt Blake ruled out the idea of Weathers’ first game back coming in the playoffs.
“I don’t know if ‘comfortable’ is [the right word],” Blake said, “but it might be the course of action where he’s the best option even though he hasn’t pitched in the last three or four weeks.”
As for the relievers that the Yankees have leaned on all season, David Bednar, Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick headline the group. All have been used heavily, especially Headrick.
The lefty allowed a grand slam to Nolan Arenado and saw his fastball velocity down an average of 1.3 mph during his major league-leading 79th appearance on Sunday, but he insisted that he feels fine physically. Boone also downplayed concerns over Headrick’s ongoing velocity fluctuations, though he did say that he hopes to get him and other relievers “in a good spot” with some rest ahead of the playoffs.
That said, the Yankees still haven’t been eliminated from the AL East race. They’ll keep trying to take the division from the Rays until they are.
“We’re going to show up Tuesday,” Boone said, “and try and kick their butt.”

PHOENIX — Los Yankees se han pasado todo el mes de septiembre intentando convertir su clasificación para la postemporada en una plantilla más clara de cara a octubre. Una de sus decisiones más difíciles de tomar ahora mismo tiene que ver con la tercera base.
Ryan McMahon llegó como un jugador que aportaba estabilidad sobre todo en defensa, pero cada vez le cuesta más ocultar su bateo. Su último bache se produjo el miércoles en el Target Field, donde se fue de 0 de 6 con cuatro strikeouts en la derrota por 5-4, en 13 entradas, ante los Minnesota Twins.
Los Yankees no dejaron de remontar. Anthony Volpe empató el partido con un doble en la novena entrada. Ali Sánchez puso a Nueva York por delante en la décima, y José Caballero sumó un fly de sacrificio en la undécima. Minnesota respondió en cada ocasión hasta que Víctor Caratini sentenció el partido con un sencillo decisivo en la 13.ª. Tommy Nance se llevó la victoria, John Schreiber la derrota y no hubo salvamento.
McMahon, que bateaba séptimo, terminó la noche con un promedio de .210/.275/.346, 10 jonrones y 34 carreras impulsadas en 118 partidos. Se ha puesto a cero 101 veces, lo que supone un porcentaje del 29,2 %, mientras que su OPS es de .621. Las estadísticas avanzadas actuales que acompañan a las críticas le sitúan en un wRC+ de 77 y un fWAR de 0,5.
Este momento hace que cada turno al bate sin resultado se note más. Los Yankees llegaban al viernes con un balance de 88-64, a cinco partidos de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, con la clasificación para la postemporada ya asegurada. Jazz Chisholm Jr. sigue en la lista de lesionados de 10 días por un esguince en el pulgar derecho, mientras que Volpe ha vuelto de la Triple A y ha jugado como segunda base.
La trayectoria de Volpe en las ligas menores ha ampliado las opciones de los Yankees. Durante su etapa en la Triple A, jugó como shortstop, segunda base y tercera base. Eso no significa que sea la solución definitiva para la tercera base, pero le da a Aaron Boone otra opción de alineación que tener en cuenta cuando vuelva Chisholm.
McMahon también tiene un sueldo garantizado de 16 millones de dólares para 2027. Los Yankees tienen que decidir si su defensa y su contrato siguen justificando que sea titular cuando la diferencia en ataque se ha vuelto tan grande.
McMahon entra en la zona de peligro de LeMahieu
Esa combinación ha hecho que cada vez más gente de los Yankees se plantee una pregunta más dura: si McMahon debería perder su puesto de titular, quedar fuera de la plantilla de la postemporada o, al final, ser designado para cesión.
La comparación que está cobrando fuerza es la de DJ LeMahieu, a quien los Yankees dejaron libre en julio de 2025 cuando aún le quedaban por cobrar unos 22 millones de dólares. Según FanGraphs, en su última temporada con los Yankees, LeMahieu registró un wRC+ de 94, un porcentaje de embasado de 0,338 y una tasa de strikeouts del 24,6 %.
McMahon está por debajo de todos esos indicadores ofensivos. Su porcentaje de llegada a base de 0,275 y su tasa de strikeouts del 29,2 % hacen que los Yankees obtengan menos aportación ofensiva de la que recibían de LeMahieu antes de decidir que ya no encajaba en su plantilla.
Las situaciones no son iguales. LeMahieu tenía 36 años, su papel se había reducido y Nueva York quería a Chisholm en segunda base. McMahon es más joven y sigue aportando valor en tercera base. Pero la decisión sobre LeMahieu dejó claro que el dinero garantizado no siempre protege el puesto de un veterano en la plantilla.
Boone sigue centrándose en el grupo
Los Yankees no han dicho públicamente que McMahon vaya a quedar fuera de la plantilla. Tras asegurarse el título, Boone habló de cómo el vestuario había afrontado una temporada difícil, en lugar de dar a entender que se hubiera tomado ninguna decisión sobre un veterano.
«Pero hay que reconocerles el mérito de haberse mantenido unidos. A pesar de todos los altibajos, han sido un grupo muy unido», dijo Boone.
Ese comentario no aclara cuál será el papel de McMahon en octubre. Lo que sí hace es resaltar la diferencia entre las presiones externas para que lo echen y la decisión que los Yankees hayan tomado realmente.
La defensa ya no es la respuesta definitiva
El argumento más sólido de McMahon sigue siendo su guante. La instantánea que te he pasado muestra un DRS de -1 y un Fielding Run Value de +1, mientras que la página en directo de Statcast muestra un valor defensivo global ligeramente positivo. La cifra exacta varía según la métrica y el momento de la actualización, pero la ventaja defensiva no oculta un OPS de 0,621.
Un tercera base con un OPS de 0,621 puede seguir siendo una opción válida si su defensa es de primera y el resto de la alineación está en forma. Los Yankees tienen menos margen mientras Chisholm esté de baja, y en octubre cada puesto de la alineación cobra más importancia.
Volpe no es un tercera base contrastado en las Grandes Ligas, y los Yankees no han dado a entender que tengan pensado darle esa posición. Aun así, su reciente actuación en esa posición en la Triple A le da a Boone una alternativa real. Su experiencia como campocorto hace que la objeción sobre la potencia de su brazo no sea tan sencilla, pero eso no garantiza que vaya a defender bien la tercera base en octubre.
La comparación de Okamoto hay que ponerla en contexto
Otra comparación que circula entre los aficionados de los Yankees compara a McMahon con el tercera base de Toronto, Kazuma Okamoto. Según la MLB, Okamoto tiene un promedio de bateo de 0,235, con 33 jonrones, 88 carreras impulsadas y un OPS de 0,774. Su contrato de cuatro años y 60 millones de dólares tiene un valor medio anual de 15 millones de dólares.
McMahon gana 16 millones de dólares y lleva 10 jonrones con un OPS de 0,621. A primera vista, el contraste es enorme.
No se trata de una decisión de la directiva en la que se pueda comparar a uno con otro sin más. McMahon ya tenía contrato cuando los Yankees lo ficharon en 2025, mientras que Okamoto llegó a la MLB siguiendo un camino diferente como agente libre. Aun así, la comparación salarial ayuda a entender por qué se han intensificado las críticas y por qué algunas de ellas se han extendido hasta el director general, Brian Cashman.
Octubre obliga a los Yankees a decidirse por un papel
No hay indicios confirmados de que los Yankees hayan decidido designar a McMahon para cesión o sacarlo de la plantilla de la postemporada. Sigue en activo, y la incertidumbre sobre la fecha de regreso de Chisholm hace que la situación en el cuadro siga siendo incierta.
Pero la cuestión ya no es si McMahon está pasando por una mala racha. Es cuánto tiempo de juego pueden permitirse los Yankees darle a un bateador con un wRC+ de 77 cuando empiece octubre.
Nueva York comienza este viernes una serie de tres partidos en el Chase Field contra Arizona. McMahon tiene tiempo para cambiar el rumbo, pero los Yankees ahora tienen menos margen de maniobra y más alternativas en el cuadro que hace un mes.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

It wouldn't have been a proper Yankees-Twins series in Minnesota without a game that devolved into extra-innings madness. The Yankees failed to cash in multiple bases loaded opportunities and so missed a chance to sweep, falling farther behind the Rays in the standings. Nonetheless, the Bombers took care of business in the first two games of the series, and it is from the middle game that we pull our candidate for Sequence of the Week.
We join Max Fried with two outs in the bottom of the fifth on Tuesday at Target Field. The Yankees have a 3-1 lead courtesy of a Cody Bellinger two-run homer and George Lombard Jr. RBI single. However, the Twins are threatening to cut the lead to one with Emmanuel Rodriguez on second with a two-out double. That brings the number nine hitter Austin Martin to the plate, a batter Fried absolutely wants to retire to avoid the lineup turning over with a runner in scoring position.
After going almost all fastballs the first time he faced Martin, Fried looks to steal a called first-pitch strike with a backdoor sweeper.
After seeing mostly hard stuff that moved away from him, you can understand why Martin would give up on this pitch early given how far from the strike zone it is initially aimed. Fried sweeps in a dandy on the outer half for called strike one.
Establishing that backdoor breaking ball for a called strike forces Martin to respect any pitches that start away, even those that look like balls out of the hand. This opens up a host of possibilities for Fried, including the changeup low and away for chase.
This is a pretty well-executed changeup out of the zone down and outside. It looks like it is aimed at that corner of the zone before fading away from the hitter. You can see Martin was initially tempted to chase the pitch — a product of that first pitch backdoor sweeper — before holding up for an impressively disciplined take.
With Martin taking against that last pitch away, Fried and Ali Sánchez feel that there is an opening for another backdoor sweeper.
Another decently executed pitch, just a little too low to nip the bottom of the zone for a second called strike. It is worth noting that Martin showed some willingness to offer before backing off, so that outside pitch is still open for chase opportunities.
Not wanting to fall any further behind in the count, Fried throws his first fastball of the encounter. However, unlike the four-seamers and sinkers he threw Martin in the first AB, this cutter breaks toward the hitter instead of away. Therefore, if the hitter succeeds in reading fastball spin out of the hand, a backdoor cutter that starts off the plate away should freeze Martin.
That is precisely what happens, Fried pinpointing this cutter with precision on the corner up and away. Martin leaves the bat on his shoulder, only to watch the pitch cut across the black of the plate for called strike two.
Now that he has established his fastball in the zone and has the count leverage in his favor, Fried has an opening to climb the ladder with the cutter hoping for a chase and whiff under a pitch elevated above the zone.
Even though this offering misses the top of the zone by about a foot, it's not a complete waste pitch. Fried has reset the hitter's eye level for the fastball up, which should open the door for a breaking ball down and in.
That is just what Fried's thought process is with the count full. He doesn't need to give in with a fastball with first base open, knowing that it will be very hard for Martin to lay off a breaking ball that looks like a strike out of the hand.
Now this is what you call a back-foot sweeper. The pitch looks like a strike for much of its journey toward home until the lateral sweep really seems to accelerate in the final 15 feet. It's just where you want to land a pitch like this, close enough to the strike zone to extract the chase but close enough to the batter that he is not able to pull in his hands in time to make contact.
Here's the full sequence:
Asked after the start what positives he would take away, Fried cited breaking ball command and an economical pitch count to go seven strong on just 88 pitches, the first point certainly highlighted by this sequence.
The Yankees desperately needed this start from Fried, not only to boost their chances of winning this particular game but also as a sign of continued build-up from the recurrence of his left elbow bone bruise. Fried labored in the start before this one, needing 80 pitches to complete 3.1 innings. Seeing him back to his best when it comes to pitch efficiency and damage limitation has to be encouraging as they formulate their postseason rotation plans.

item.content:encoded:
MINNEAPOLIS — Anthony Volpe bateó con tanta fuerza que perdió el equilibrio, convencido de que la pelota se había ido fuera. En cambio, rebotó contra el muro alto del centro-derecha, un doble de dos carreras que igualó el marcador para los Yankees con dos outs en la novena entrada. Durante un momento intenso y emocionante el miércoles, Nueva York parecía dispuesta a llevarse la barrida.
Lo que vino después fueron cuatro entradas más en las que el equipo llegaba hasta la puerta y se negaba a cruzarla. Los Yankees se pusieron por delante en la décima. Volvieron a hacerlo en la undécima. Llenaron las bases sin outs en la duodécima. Cada vez acababan con un empate o con una remontada desperdiciada.
Un viaje que debería haber acabado con una barrida acabó poniendo de manifiesto el único punto débil que un aspirante al título no puede permitirse arrastrar hasta octubre. No se trató de un colapso del bullpen ni de un rebote desafortunado. Fue la alineación de los Yankees la que no paraba de preparar la mesa, pero nunca se sentaba a comer.
La culpa final recayó en un novato que no se la merecía él solo.
Los Minnesota Twins vencieron a los Yankees por 5-4 en 13 entradas, poniendo fin a ese partido maratoniano con un sencillo de Victor Caratini en la primera base que rebotó en el montículo y se coló por debajo del guante de George Lombard Jr. en la segunda base. Con esta derrota, Nueva York queda con un balance de 88-64, a cuatro partidos de los Rays de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, a falta de 10 partidos por disputar. Los Yankees ya tienen asegurada su plaza en los playoffs, pero el título de la división y la exención de la primera ronda se les están escapando.
Una remontada que no llevó a ninguna parte
Nueva York había sumado cuatro hits en ocho entradas y perdía por 2-0, mientras que el lanzador diestro de los Twins, Zebby Matthews, había ponchado a ocho. Entonces llegó la novena entrada. Lombard conectó un sencillo, Paul Goldschmidt le siguió y el corredor suplente José Caballero preparó el terreno para Volpe.
Volpe impulsó las dos carreras, lo que le supuso al cerrador de los Twins, Yoendrys Gómez, su primer salvamento fallido del año y obligó a jugar entradas extras.
Ali Sánchez impulsó al corredor automático con un sencillo en la décima entrada, dando a los Yankees su primera ventaja. Luke Keaschall respondió con un sencillo que empató el partido ante David Bednar. Un fly de sacrificio de Caballero puso a Nueva York por delante en la undécima. Royce Lewis igualó el marcador. Dos ventajas, dos respuestas inmediatas.
La entrada que dará que hablar
La 12.ª es la entrada que los aficionados volverán a ver una y otra vez. Los Yankees llenaron las bases sin outs, la situación que debería haber sentenciado el partido. Pero no sacaron nada de ella.
Heliot Ramos, que bateaba en el turno de Aaron Judge, mandó una bola corta hacia el montículo. Travis Adams la convirtió en una doble jugada 1-2-3. Sánchez se fue con un strikeout, dejando a otros dos en base. Los Yankees acabaron con 7 de 30 con corredores en posición de anotar.
El juez se marcha y el ataque se queda con pocos jugadores
Judge se retiró en la sexta entrada por una contractura en la parte inferior de la pierna derecha que empezó a notar en la primera entrada. Falló dos veces y no volvió al campo, solo siete partidos después de una ausencia de 99 días. Por eso Ramos estaba bateando en su lugar.
El entrenador Aaron Boone describió la noche como una oportunidad perdida, no como un partido robado, y sus palabras reflejaban la importancia del momento en el calendario.
«Obviamente, muchas cosas buenas, pero no las suficientes», dijo Boone. «Ha sido un golpe duro, claro, cuando tenías la oportunidad de barrer la serie y justo antes de un día de descanso. Pero tenemos que superarlo y prepararnos para enfrentarnos a un buen equipo de los Diamondbacks».
Al final del partido, Boone no se anduvo con rodeos con Lombard, pero tampoco lo machacó.
Boone reconoció que la bola de Caratini rebotó en el montículo, pero fue una jugada que Lombard «se espera que haga y sabemos que es capaz de hacer».
Rodón lo da todo en octubre, pero no saca nada a cambio
Carlos Rodón le dio a los Yankees el comienzo que necesita una rotación en la postemporada y vio cómo se esfumaba. El zurdo encajó dos carreras en seis entradas, ampliando su récord de la franquicia a 25 salidas consecutivas en las que ha encajado tres carreras o menos. Lanzó 102 lanzamientos, su máximo de la temporada, y bajó su promedio de carreras limpias a 2,95.
«Empecé un poco lento, un poco tenso», dijo Rodon. «Me fui soltando en las siguientes entradas, así que eso estuvo bien».
Clarke Schmidt hizo su tan esperado regreso en la séptima entrada, ponchando a dos antes de que Brent Headrick dejara a dos en base. El bullpen corrió una maratón que la alineación nunca supo recompensar.
Una primicia para el club que no se veía desde 1991
Este es el dato que pocos destacarán. Ha sido la primera derrota de los Yankees tras ir ganando varias veces en entradas extras desde el 5 de mayo de 1991, en Seattle, es decir, en un lapso de más de 34 años. También fue su octava derrota en la última entrada de la temporada, un récord de la franquicia, y ningún equipo de la MLB ha encajado más hits decisivos en la última entrada en 2026, según datos de Baseball Reference. Ningún equipo de los Yankees ha perdido nunca más partidos a domicilio en entradas extras en una sola temporada.
Lo curioso es que los equipos malos no acumulan cifras como estas. Un equipo mediocre pierde en nueve partidos. Solo un buen equipo es capaz de forzar una prórroga fuera de casa una y otra vez, y luego seguir perdiéndola.
Cómo queda la carrera por la División Este de la Liga Americana
Spencer Jones lanzó su propia advertencia, ponchándose cinco veces en una noche en la que se fue de 0 de 6, lo que demostró lo rápido que se castigan los swings fallidos cuando los márgenes se estrechan. En septiembre se lee de otra manera que en julio.
Los Yankees tienen el jueves libre antes de empezar una serie de fin de semana en Arizona, donde Gerrit Cole será el lanzador titular el viernes a las 21:40 h (hora del Este). No se espera que Judge tenga que hacerse más pruebas. Nueva York ha perdido terreno que quizá no recupere y le ha dado un respiro a los Rays.
Los Yankees saben cómo ganar los partidos intermedios. Una noche en la que solo tenían que ganar uno, no pudieron.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are now in wait-and-see mode.
Aaron Judge left Wednesday’s game early with right leg tightness. There’s no word yet on whether he’ll have to miss time, and we likely won’t have an answer until Friday at the earliest.
Before then, let’s answer some of your Yankees questions in part one of our mailbag. If you want to ask anything else, there’s still time to do so here.
Note: Questions have been edited for clarity and brevity.
Advertisement
Assuming Trent Grisham is healthy, who starts in center field during the playoffs: him or Spencer Jones? — Ed H.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters Wednesday that Grisham is running “up to a decent speed” in his comeback from a right hamstring strain. Considering Grisham at normal speed is slow, it’s anyone’s guess what that actually means.
If Grisham is ready to go, it will be interesting to see what Boone decides. There are numerous examples of the Yankees opting for the veteran over an inexperienced player like Jones when the games matter most.
Both players have their warts. Neither Grisham nor Jones is a good defensive center fielder. Jones looked abysmal in center, letting a ground ball go under his glove, dropping a fly ball that hit his glove and nearly trucking Heliot Ramos in right field. Meanwhile, Grisham has trouble getting to balls over his head and in the gaps because he’s slow-footed. There’s likely a higher floor of success, though, for Grisham. Even on the balls Jones has caught, there have been instances where he doesn’t look comfortable reading the play off the bat.
So the main difference will come down to offense.
Before Grisham injured his hamstring, he was not hitting. Calls for Jones to take over were already happening. To Jones’ credit, he has produced at the plate. Even after a dreadful 0-for-6 performance with five strikeouts on Wednesday, Jones has a 113 wRC+. He is always a threat to pop a home run, and that wins ballgames in October.
Grisham has one of the best eyes on the team, rarely strikes out and works at-bats. That matters when the batters behind him would likely be Ben Rice and Judge (depending on his health).
Not that my opinion holds any weight, but I’d stick with Jones in center field. The Yankees can always use Grisham, who’s one of the most clutch hitters on the team, in big spots off the bench.
Advertisement
What will/should the Yankees playoff rotation and bullpen look like? I hate to say it, but Gerrit Cole and Max Fried are not looking like aces these days. The team is winning Will Warren’s and Carlos Rodón’s starts. How are these facts likely to influence Boone’s postseason rotation decisions? … As soon as I say this, Fried pitches a gem. Jinx. — Aaron D.
The American League East race isn’t over yet, but the likeliest outcome is the Yankees will play in a wild-card series against the Boston Red Sox. That means the Yankees will only need three starting pitchers for the first round.
Cam Schlittler should start Game 1. There’s no argument otherwise. Schlittler is one of the very best starting pitchers in the sport. You want your best pitcher going in Game 1 to give yourself the best possible chance of not facing a must-win Game 2.
From there, it’ll be a toss-up between Fried and Cole. Both pitchers have concerns attached to them.
Fried has battled command issues all season, while Cole has allowed plenty of hard contact while not getting much swing-and-miss. I’d lean toward Fried over Cole.
As for the bullpen, the Yankees could have Rodón in case the club needs length. The others likely to be on the roster are Will Warren, David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, John Schreiber, Clarke Schmidt, Ryan Yarbrough and Ryan Weathers, if he’s healthy. I’d leave off Tim Hill, who has struggled mightily this season, Luis Gil and Michael Fulmer.
What is the realistic outlook for second base next year? Jazz Chisholm Jr. hasn’t played up to his talent, which might make him more enticing by bringing down his cost. The infield is already crowded, though, with Ryan McMahon under contract, George Lombard Jr.’s promotion, José Caballero, two first basemen (three if Paul Goldschmidt is still seen as Giancarlo Stanton insurance), and Anthony Volpe’s re-ascension. — Marco F.
What the Yankees decide to do at second base is one of the most fascinating storylines of the offseason.
Advertisement
I agree with you, Marco, that this season has likely cost Chisholm millions. He is nearing the end of his worst offensive season since 2021. He won’t reach the heights he set for himself entering 2026, but he still could reach a 20-40 season. Few players have the talent to post those numbers. Before this year, Chisholm posted back-to-back 4+ fWAR seasons. It would not be wrong for the Yankees or another team to bet on his upside.
Chisholm still offers tremendous defense at second and excellent baserunning. If his bat gets back to being considerably above average, he profiles as one of the best second basemen in the sport. There are valid concerns about his offense, though. His hit tool is considerably below average, and as he ages and loses athleticism, that could be a major problem that he cannot overcome.
The Yankees should consider giving Chisholm a short-term deal, though. He is a better option than Caballero and Volpe, who are better as role players, and few available players are better than what he can provide.
The Yankees should strongly consider playing Caballero or Volpe, who played a few games in the minors there, at third base. McMahon is one of the worst everyday regulars in the big leagues this season, and there’s a higher likelihood of Caballero or Volpe producing at the plate.
Has the Martian played his last game in a Yankees uniform? — oconnell13
It’s a hard question to answer because you can’t predict injuries. You never know if the Yankees will have to reach into the minor leagues for depth.
But it’s not far-fetched to think Jasson Domínguez will never play in another important game for the Yankees again. He cannot be trusted in the field. Every game matters for the Yankees, and there’s always a queasy feeling when the ball is hit his way.
His bat also hasn’t progressed enough to keep giving him chances to prove himself. Jones has leapfrogged him on the depth chart, and the Yankees now have Heliot Ramos on their roster. There may not be space for Domínguez.
Advertisement
What are the Yankees’ pitching plans for the rest of the regular season? Specifically, who’s lining up for the Rays series and will any of them be limited in terms of pitch count? — Nick B.
As of now, the Yankees are lined up to start their best four starters against the Rays next week. Here’s how it looks:
Tuesday: Fried and Rodón are in line to start the games of the doubleheader.
Wednesday: Cole
Thursday: Schlittler
The Rays are also on track to start their best pitchers for that series. They could start Nick Martinez and Drew Rasmussen on Tuesday, Freddy Peralta on Wednesday and Ian Seymour on Thursday. Their rotation is dependent on what they decide to do for their weekend series against the Boston Red Sox. But if they wanted, all of these pitchers could factor into their pitching plans next week.
Any chance the Yanks consider Ben Rice as the backup catcher on the postseason roster to free up an extra bench spot for someone more versatile (and better than) Ali Sánchez/J.C. Escarra? — Matthew L.
The odds of this happening are close to zero.
Earlier in the season, Rice kept catching behind the scenes. Before games, he’d catch bullpens and do on-field drills with director of catching Tanner Swanson. Rice hasn’t done any of that in months.
If anything, Rice would only be used in an emergency situation. Believe it or not, the organization believes in Sánchez. That’s why they didn’t promote Mitch Garver. Sánchez is out of minor league options, so they’d have to designate him for assignment and risk him getting claimed off waivers. They value the consistency he provides to their pitchers, and they think he’s a better defender than the metrics show.

MINNEAPOLIS -- The first two games of this week’s series at Target Field couldn’t have gone much better for the Yankees. They won both handily, and on Monday Aaron Judge hit his first home run since returning from the IL on Sept. 8.
Judge, who sat out Tuesday’s game as a routine day off after playing six straight games, struck out in each of his first two at-bats against Twins starter Zebby Matthews on Wednesday. After the game, he said he felt a stiffness in his lower right leg in the first inning.
“I tried to kind of play it off and see how long we could go, because these games are important down the stretch,” Judge said. “But kind of talking it over, I thought it'd be the right move to come out, so I don't cost the team on the field or cost the team on the basepath.”
With an off-day scheduled for Thursday, the team will wait to issue any prognosis on the severity of the injury until after he’s received extensive treatment over the next 48 hours.
“We’re not going to speculate one way or the other. We’ll just see how he responds,” manager Aaron Boone said.
Judge, who said he didn’t anticipate getting testing done, said he couldn’t pinpoint any specific activity or movement that triggered the stiffness, but the feeling isn’t an unfamiliar one to him.
“I feel like you deal with this every Spring Training. You know, usually at the start of the season once you start ramping up again, things pop up, and that's where we've been,” Judge said. “Thankfully, this whole time coming back, nothing's really nagged us. So hopefully it's just one little thing and then we're back out there soon.”
It would be a huge blow to the team to lose Judge after just getting him back into the lineup for the first time in three months. But at the same time, professional athletes and their coaches have to keep an eye on the big picture, and one Wednesday afternoon game against the Twins in mid-September pales in importance compared to upcoming series against the Diamondbacks, Rays and Orioles, plus whatever postseason action the team might see.
That’s especially true when that four-game series against Tampa Bay starting Tuesday could still determine the AL East champions -- and potentially a first-round bye in the postseason.
“Obviously he’s a key figure of what we do,” Boone said. “Hopefully we get it treated and knock it out and be a factor at some point.”
Heliot Ramos pinch-hit for Judge and also struck out against Matthews, who fanned eight in six scoreless innings. Ramos would likely fill in for Judge in right field during any absence he might incur.
The Yankees certainly could have used Judge’s bat in the lineup as they traded blows with the Twins in extra innings, after Anthony Volpe smacked a game-tying double off the wall in the top of the ninth with his club down to its final out.
In the 12th, the Yanks squandered an opportunity with the bases loaded and nobody out, as Ramos grounded into a double play, with Volpe thrown out at home plate. Ali Sánchez then struck out to end the threat, before Twins pinch-hitter Victor Caratini delivered a walk-off single up the middle in the 13th.

They’re coming off an 8-1 victory over the Twins on Tuesday night in a game in which infielder Anthony Volpe recorded two hits to continue his strong stretch since being recalled on Sept. 10.
However, ahead of Wednesday’s game, Yankees manager Aaron Boone decided to make a notable lineup move involving Volpe.
Yankees Announce Volpe Move
After spending his last few games batting in the seven-hole and clearly adapting just fine at the plate, Boone has decided to move Volpe back down to the nine spot for the series finale.
Other notable lineup changes include superstar Aaron Judge rejoining the lineup after a night off, catcher Austin Wells replacing Ali Sanchez behind the plate, and Jose Caballero getting the day off.

It’s been a challenging 2026 season for Volpe, who’s in his fourth year with the Yankees.

MINNEAPOLIS — Apenas se había secado el champán cuando los Yankees se enfrentaron a la pregunta que quedaba pendiente desde la noche anterior: ¿Aparecería sin energía un equipo que se había pasado la noche de fiesta hasta altas horas de la madrugada?
Pues no fue así.
Cody Bellinger conectó un jonrón de dos carreras en la primera entrada; los Yankees terminaron con 14 hits —cada titular consiguió al menos uno— y Nueva York nunca estuvo por detrás en el marcador en la victoria por 8-1 sobre los Twins en el Target Field el martes.
Pero la cifra que más importaba para los Yankees en octubre era el número de lanzamientos de Max Fried.
Tras una salida en la que le costó mucho completar 3 1/3 entradas contra Colorado, Fried lanzó siete entradas con 88 lanzamientos, cediendo una carrera y seis hits, con seis strikeouts y ninguna base por bolas. Fue su salida más larga desde el 22 de abril y su primera victoria desde el 27 de abril. En Colorado, el lanzador de los Yankees necesitó 80 lanzamientos para conseguir 10 outs. El martes, solo necesitó ocho más para lograr 21.
Fried dijo que un pequeño ajuste en el control de sus lanzamientos lentos lo cambió todo.
Cómo los Yankees sentenciaron el partido desde el principio
Después de que Dean Kremer les limitara a dos hits, los Yankees se lanzaron a por Bailey Ober. Ben Rice, tras estar a punto de recibir un pelotazo, abrió la entrada con un sencillo. Bellinger le siguió con su decimosexto jonrón al centro-derecha.
Bellinger conectó 3 de 4 con una base por bolas y lleva un promedio de bateo de 0,377 en sus últimos 17 partidos, con cinco jonrones desde que volvió tras una lesión en el tendón de la corva. El promedio del bateador de los Yankees subió a 0,272, su mejor marca desde el 22 de junio.
Anthony Volpe y Ali Sánchez conectaron dos sencillos seguidos en la segunda entrada, pero Ober dejó a ambos en base. Minnesota respondió cuando Royce Lewis llegó a base con un sencillo al cuadro, robó la segunda y anotó gracias a un sencillo impulsor de Emmanuel Rodríguez con dos outs. Fried zanjó la jugada con un pickoff de libro contra Rodríguez.
Los Yankees respondieron en la tercera entrada. Heliot Ramos consiguió una base por bolas, Luis García Jr. conectó un sencillo y George Lombard Jr. bateó un sencillo impulsador con dos outs por la banda derecha, poniendo el marcador 3-1 a su favor. Volpe consiguió otra base por bolas y llenó las bases, pero el batazo de Sánchez al centro se quedó en la zona de advertencia.
Ober repartió nueve hits a lo largo de 5 1/3 entradas y encajó tres carreras, mientras Nueva York dejaba a sus corredores en las bases una y otra vez. Eso cambió en la sexta.
Rice llegó a base por un error del campocorto Kaelen Culpepper, Bellinger consiguió una base por bolas tras cuatro lanzamientos y Ramos conectó un doble ante el zurdo Taylor Rogers para poner el 4-1 en el marcador.
Le tocó el turno a Spencer Jones. Tras fallar una serie de lanzamientos bajos y lentos, el bateador novato de los Yankees conectó el cuarto, que le llegó justo por el centro con una cuenta de 2-2, y lo mandó 423 pies al centro para un jonrón de tres carreras, poniendo el marcador 7-1.
Rogers no había cedido ningún jonrón a un bateador zurdo en toda la temporada, en 133 turnos al bate. Jones puso fin a esa racha. Ahora tiene un promedio de bateo de .435/.490/.761 contra lanzadores zurdos y se ha convertido en el undécimo Yankee con más de diez jonrones esta temporada, igualando el total del club en 2019.
Las cuatro carreras de la sexta entrada fueron sucias debido a un error de Culpepper.
Nueva York sumó una carrera en la novena entrada cuando Lombard consiguió una base por bolas, avanzó gracias a un roletazo de out y anotó gracias al sencillo de José Caballero ante Andrew Morris.
Todos los titulares de los Yankees consiguieron al menos un hit y llegaron a base. Ramos, Lombard y Volpe llegaron a base tres veces cada uno. Con esta victoria, Nueva York queda con un balance de 88-63, tras encadenar siete victorias en ocho partidos y con una ventaja de seis partidos sobre Boston en la lucha por el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana.
El ajuste que hizo Fried entre sus salidas
Fried dijo que un mejor control de sus lanzamientos lentos le permitió utilizarlos en cualquier cuenta.
«Simplemente tuve más control sobre mis lanzamientos lentos. Pude lanzarlos para conseguir strikes. Siento que he podido lanzarlos en cualquier cuenta. Y tenía mucha, mucha confianza en eso. He trabajado muy bien con Ali (Sánchez) y, además, cuando tienes a la defensa haciendo grandes jugadas detrás de ti, eso te da más confianza», le dijo el as de los Yankees a Meredith Marakovits, de YES Network.
Era la novena salida de Fried desde que volvió tras su segunda baja por lesión, a causa de un hematoma óseo en el codo izquierdo. El objetivo de los Yankees era reducir el número de lanzamientos por entrada y que aguantara más tiempo en el montículo.
«La verdad es que me ha venido muy bien poder hacer lo que me ha parecido una salida completa, sin estar tan limitado por el recuento de lanzamientos», dijo Fried. «Aún así, llegué a los 88 lanzamientos y terminé la séptima entrada, así que me alegro de haber podido tachar eso de la lista. Pero es una mezcla de sentirme bien con dónde estamos y, al mismo tiempo, saber que todavía tenemos cosas en las que trabajar».
El entrenador de los Yankees, Aaron Boone, dijo que Fried podría mejorar aún más la próxima vez.
«Me gusta cómo está ahora, y espero que pueda seguir mejorando un poco más en el próximo partido y que siga así», dijo Boone. «Pero me ha encantado cómo ha atacado la zona de strike, cómo ha controlado los conteos y cómo ha tenido mucha presencia con la mayoría de sus lanzamientos esta noche».
¿Por qué es importante el momento en octubre?
La salud y la carga de trabajo de Fried son clave para las cuentas de los Yankees de cara a la postemporadahttps://pinstripesnation.com/mlb-2026-postseason-schedule-yankees-2026-08-11/. Tras el partido del martes, tenía una efectividad de 2,63 y, desde el parón del All-Star, acumula una efectividad de 1,83 con 50 strikeouts en 44 1/3 entradas en nueve partidos como titular.
Los datos sobre los lanzamientos coinciden. Según un gráfico de Pitch Profiler, Fried lanzó su «sweeper» 19 veces, lo que supone el 21,6 % de sus 88 lanzamientos. Los bateadores fallaron el golpe en el 70 % de las ocasiones y obtuvieron un promedio de embasado ponderado esperado de 0,098.
Su bola curva, lanzada 15 veces, generó un porcentaje de fallos del 33,3 %. El cambio de velocidad del as de los Yankees , lanzado 13 veces, generó un porcentaje de fallos del 37,5 % y un promedio esperado de .175.
Esos tres lanzamientos lentos supusieron 47 de sus 88 lanzamientos, más de la mitad de su carga de trabajo. Esa confianza en sus lanzamientos secundarios le ayudó a conseguir una tasa global de strikes fallidos del 32,6 %, sin conceder bases por bolas. La bola rápida de cuatro costuras y la sinker de la estrella de los Yankees le dieron los peores resultados, y fueron los que menos utilizó.
Ahora viene una prueba más dura.
Fried se enfrentará a los Rays la semana que viene en uno de los dos partidos de una doble jornada que dará inicio a una serie decisiva de cuatro partidos en el Yankee Stadium. Los Yankees siguen a 3 1/2 partidos del Tampa Bay (91-59) en la División Este de la Liga Americana, a falta de 11 partidos por disputar.
«Va a ser béisbol de eliminatorias», dijo Fried. «Son dos equipos, dos equipos realmente buenos, que van a darlo todo. Estoy deseando formar parte de esto y no veo la hora de que llegue la semana que viene».
¿Qué le parece? Deje su comentario a continuación.

Looking at Wells

Wells will be looking to keep his hot streak at the plate going once he returns to New York’s lineup. In 115 games this season for New York, he has posted 12 home runs, 30 RBI, and a .180 batting average.
Looking at the Yankees Right Now
The Yankees have an 87-63 record and are 3.5 games behind the first-place Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East.
New York has won seven out of their last 10 games and recently clinched a playoff spot. With this, the vibes are high with New York right now, and they will be looking to finish the season on a high note.
